options.content:
### SWIFT Networking

Router capacity SLI and the supporting SWIFT NIC-assignment, CNS, and Konnectivity telemetry for a management cluster.

**Sections:**
- **Alert SLI** — the series and threshold lines that the `userJourneySwiftRouterAvailability*` alerts evaluate.
- **Router Replicas and Pods** — router replica counts, Pending age, and pod readiness per HCP namespace.
- **Node and NIC Capacity** — node readiness, SWIFT NIC capacity, pending IP programming, and node-health detector labels.
- **CNS** — CNS DaemonSet pods, IP-assignment latency, and IP-assignment outcomes.
- **Konnectivity Tunnel** — per-HCP backend, error, dial-failure, and packet telemetry.

**Alert SLI definition:** a minute is bad (`swift_router_capacity:degraded` = 1) when some HCP on the management cluster has had a router replica missing for 10 minutes or longer. The SLI is good minutes divided by eligible minutes, against a 99.95% objective over 28 days. Each burn-rate panel plots the trailing bad-minute count for its alert windows with threshold lines at the alert limits; the plotted series continue past the lines.

**Filters:**
- Select a management cluster to scope every panel.
- Optionally select one or more HCP namespaces to narrow the per-HCP router and Konnectivity panels. CNS and node panels are scoped to the management cluster or node because their telemetry carries no HCP identity.

**Datasources:**
- Router and Konnectivity panels use the **HCP AMW** (`Managed_Prometheus_hcps-*`).
- CNS and node panels use the **services AMW** (`Managed_Prometheus_services-*`); the requested-NIC series on the SWIFT NIC panel uses the HCP AMW.

**Usage:** start with [SWIFT TSG: Establish Blast Radius](https://aka.ms/arohcp-tsg-swift#step-1-establish-blast-radius) when an alert fires, then read the panels below for the management cluster and HCP namespaces involved.

panels.description: Per-minute flag recorded by `swift_router_capacity:degraded`: 1 while some HCP on the management cluster has had a router replica missing for 10 minutes or longer, 0 otherwise. One series per management cluster.
panels.title: Router Capacity Bad Minutes (swift_router_capacity:degraded)

panels.description: Good minutes divided by eligible minutes over the trailing 28 days (or the available history), computed as 1 minus the average of `swift_router_capacity:degraded`. The line marks the 99.95% objective.
panels.title: Router Capacity SLI (rolling 28d)

panels.description: Remaining share of the 28-day error budget for the 99.95% objective: ((SLI − 0.9995) / 0.0005) × 100, computed from `swift_router_capacity:degraded`. The value continues below 0 when the budget is overspent. The line marks 0.
panels.title: Error Budget Remaining (rolling 28d)

panels.description: Management-cluster router replica totals: `swift_router_replicas:configured`, `swift_router_replicas:available`, and `swift_router_replicas:unavailable_sustained` (replicas missing from HCPs whose router Deployment has been short for 11 consecutive 1-minute samples).
panels.title: Router Replica Totals

panels.description: Bad minutes (`swift_router_capacity:degraded` = 1) in the trailing window, one series per management cluster and window. The `userJourneySwiftRouterAvailability1h5m` alert condition holds when both windows exceed their dashed alert threshold series. Each threshold equals 14.4 × 0.05% × the eligible minutes in that window (0.432 for a full 1h window, 0.036 for a full 5m window).
panels.title: Fast Burn (1h/5m): Bad Minutes in Window

panels.description: Bad minutes (`swift_router_capacity:degraded` = 1) in the trailing window, one series per management cluster and window. The `userJourneySwiftRouterAvailability6h30m` alert condition holds when both windows exceed their dashed alert threshold series. Each threshold equals 6 × 0.05% × the eligible minutes in that window (1.08 for a full 6h window, 0.09 for a full 30m window).
panels.title: Medium Burn (6h/30m): Bad Minutes in Window

panels.description: Bad minutes (`swift_router_capacity:degraded` = 1) in the trailing window, one series per management cluster and window. The `userJourneySwiftRouterAvailability3d6h` alert condition holds when both windows exceed their dashed alert threshold series. Each threshold equals 1 × 0.05% × the eligible minutes in that window (2.16 for a full 3d window, 0.18 for a full 6h window).
panels.title: Slow Burn (3d/6h): Bad Minutes in Window

panels.description: Router replicas missing per HCP namespace: `kube_deployment_spec_replicas` minus `kube_deployment_status_replicas_available` for the `router` Deployment, shown while the value is above zero.

targets.expr: (max by (cluster, namespace) (kube_deployment_spec_replicas{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$hcp_namespace", deployment="router"}) - max by (cluster, namespace) (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$hcp_namespace", deployment="router"})) > 0

panels.title: Router Replicas Missing (by HCP namespace)

panels.description: Number of 1-minute samples in the trailing 30 minutes in which the HCP's router Deployment had a replica missing. The alert counts an HCP once 11 consecutive samples show a missing replica; the line marks 11.

targets.expr: count_over_time(((max by (cluster, namespace) (kube_deployment_spec_replicas{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$hcp_namespace", deployment="router"}) - max by (cluster, namespace) (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$hcp_namespace", deployment="router"})) > 0)[30m:1m])

panels.title: Minutes With Router Replicas Missing, Last 30m (by HCP namespace)

panels.description: Age of each router pod while it is `Pending`, from `router:startup_latency:seconds`. A series exists while its pod is Pending.
panels.title: Router Pod Pending Age (by pod)

panels.description: Router pods whose `Ready` condition is false, with the node they run on, from `kube_pod_status_ready{condition="false"}` joined with `kube_pod_info`.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_ready{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$hcp_namespace", pod=~"router-.*", condition="false"} == 1) * on (cluster, namespace, pod) group_left (node) max by (cluster, namespace, pod, node) (kube_pod_info{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$hcp_namespace", pod=~"router-.*"})

panels.title: Router Pods With Ready Condition False

panels.description: SWIFT NIC resources per management-cluster worker node with `resource="aro_openshift_io_swift_nic"`: `kube_node_status_capacity` and `kube_node_status_allocatable` from the services AMW, and the sum of `kube_pod_container_resource_requests` for pods on the node from the HCP AMW, with one series per container (deduplicated across scrape replicas).

targets.expr: max by (cluster, node) (kube_node_status_capacity{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"aks-user.*", resource="aro_openshift_io_swift_nic"})
max by (cluster, node) (kube_node_status_allocatable{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"aks-user.*", resource="aro_openshift_io_swift_nic"})
sum by (cluster, node) (max by (cluster, namespace, pod, container, node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", resource="aro_openshift_io_swift_nic"}))

panels.title: SWIFT NIC Capacity, Allocatable, and Requested (by node)

panels.description: Node `Ready` condition per management-cluster worker node in the `aks-user*` pools, from `kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready", status="true"}` (1 = Ready).

targets.expr: max by (cluster, node) (kube_node_status_condition{job="kube-state-metrics", cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"aks-user.*", condition="Ready", status="true"})

panels.title: Node Ready Condition (by node)

panels.description: Reserved IPs awaiting secondary-NIC attachment, from `cx_pending_programming_ips_v2`. One series per CNS pod (management-cluster worker node).
panels.title: Pending IP Programming (by CNS pod)

panels.description: Nodes currently labeled by the mgmt-agent `swift-vf-teardown` detector, from `nodehealth_node_wedged{detector="swift-vf-teardown"}`, with the label signature.
panels.title: Node-Health Detector Labels (swift-vf-teardown)

panels.description: Ratio of ready to desired `azure-cns` DaemonSet pods on the management cluster, from `cns:daemonset_availability:ratio`.
panels.title: CNS DaemonSet Ready / Desired Pods Ratio

panels.description: p99 latency of successful CNS secondary IP assignments on the management cluster, from `cns:ip_assignment_latency:p99`. The histogram records successful assignments.
panels.title: CNS IP Assignment Latency p99

panels.description: Management-cluster-wide CNS RequestIPConfig and RequestIPConfigs rates by CNS application return code (`cns_return_code`), from `http_request_latency_seconds_count`.

targets.expr: sum by (cluster, cns_return_code) (max without (prometheus_replica) (rate(http_request_latency_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", verb="POST", url=~".*/network/requestipconfigs?.*", cns_return_code!="Success"}[5m])))

panels.title: CNS IP Assignment Request Outcome Rates

panels.description: Share of CNS RequestIPConfig and RequestIPConfigs calls with `cns_return_code="Success"`. CNS returns HTTP 200 for application outcomes.

targets.expr: ((sum by (cluster) (max without (prometheus_replica) (rate(http_request_latency_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", verb="POST", url=~".*/network/requestipconfigs?.*", cns_return_code="Success"}[5m]))) or 0 * sum by (cluster) (max without (prometheus_replica) (rate(http_request_latency_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", verb="POST", url=~".*/network/requestipconfigs?.*"}[5m])))) / sum by (cluster) (max without (prometheus_replica) (rate(http_request_latency_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", verb="POST", url=~".*/network/requestipconfigs?.*"}[5m])))) and on (cluster) (sum by (cluster) (max without (prometheus_replica) (rate(http_request_latency_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", verb="POST", url=~".*/network/requestipconfigs?.*"}[5m]))) > 0)

panels.title: CNS IP Assignment Success Ratio

panels.description: Distinct connected Konnectivity backend identities per HCP namespace, from `konnectivity_network_proxy_server_ready_backends`. ARO-HCP worker agents share the `default-route=true` identity, so the value is 1 or more while any worker agent is connected and 0 when none is.
panels.title: Konnectivity Connected Backend Identities (by HCP namespace)

panels.description: Count of selected HCP namespaces whose connected Konnectivity backend identities total zero, from `konnectivity_network_proxy_server_ready_backends`.
panels.title: HCP Namespaces With Zero Connected Konnectivity Backends

panels.description: Konnectivity server-side gRPC control-stream errors per processed packet, from `konnectivity:stream_error_rate:5m`.
panels.title: Konnectivity Control-Stream Error Frequency

panels.description: Absolute rate of Konnectivity server-side control-stream receive errors, from `konnectivity:stream_errors:rate5m`.
panels.title: Konnectivity Control-Stream Errors per Second

panels.description: Konnectivity server-observed dial-failure frequency, from `konnectivity:dial_failure_rate:5m`. The server can increment `dial_failure_count` more than once for one dial, and a `DIAL_RSP` packet can carry an error.
panels.title: Konnectivity Dial-Failure Frequency

panels.description: Konnectivity protocol packet volume per HCP namespace, from `konnectivity_network_proxy_server_stream_packets_total`.
panels.title: Konnectivity Packet Volume (by HCP namespace)
